pipeline.title: Raw ingestion
pipeline.description: Builds the 48-team field, a pot-based group draw, latent 'true' strengths, a synthetic 2019-2025 international match history (training data) and the canonical 2026 bracket.

pipeline.title: Validation & cleaning
pipeline.description: Schema, range and referential-integrity checks; chronological ordering; outcome labelling. Fails loudly on malformed data.

pipeline.title: Feature engineering
pipeline.description: Leakage-free rolling features: Elo, recent form, goals for/against, xG trend, rest days, head-to-head, squad strength, host & stage flags.

pipeline.title: Model training
pipeline.description: Trains Elo baseline, Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost on the synthetic history ONLY (no World Cup match is ever seen in training).

pipeline.title: Prediction & simulation
pipeline.description: Per-match probabilities + explanation factors, a 20k-tournament Monte-Carlo for title odds, team metrics and player statistics.

pipeline.title: Backtest & self-improvement
pipeline.description: Scores every model against completed matches (accuracy, log-loss, Brier, calibration), re-ranks them and updates the ensemble weights (∝ 1/log-loss).

dataSources.name: 48-team field, Elo ratings & colours
dataSources.description: Curated from publicly known FIFA/Elo values and national colours. The exact qualified field is a projection.

dataSources.name: International match history 2019-2025
dataSources.description: Synthetic matches simulated from latent team strengths — used only for model training.

dataSources.name: Squads & player statistics
dataSources.description: 26 generated players per nation with culturally-plausible names, plus minutes-aware tournament stats. No real player data or headshots are used.

dataSources.name: Country flags
dataSources.description: SVG flags rendered via the open-source flag-icons library.

models.name: Elo Baseline
models.summary: Analytic two-stage Elo with a fitted draw model. A strong, transparent benchmark.

models.name: Logistic Regression
models.summary: Multinomial regression on standardised features — interpretable coefficients.

models.name: Random Forest
models.summary: Bagged decision trees capturing non-linear feature interactions.

models.name: XGBoost
models.summary: Gradient-boosted trees — typically the strongest single learner.

notes: Predictions are probabilistic estimates, not guarantees.
Models are trained only on historical (pre-tournament) data; completed matches are used exclusively for backtesting — preventing data leakage.
The Round-of-32 seeding uses a simplified strength seeding rather than FIFA's official pairing table.
Title odds come from a Monte-Carlo simulation using a calibrated Elo+squad model; per-match modal probabilities come from the full ML ensemble.
104 World Cup matches are covered end-to-end.
